insights.headline: Gold steadies near $4,072 after strong US jobs data as MCX ends Diwali Muhurat session higher
insights.summary: MCX December gold rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g and silver edged up 0.2% to Rs 1,85,079 per kg in Sunday's Diwali Muhurat session, while spot gold traded near $4,072. US payrolls rose 165,000 in October, far above the 65,000 forecast, lifting the dollar and December Fed hike odds, yet gold ended the week about 4.4% higher and silver 5.75% higher. Dhanteras sales crossed Rs 60,000 crore as a price dip drew festive demand, and the US October CPI due on Tuesday 10 November is the next big test for bullion.
points: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October, far above the 65,000 forecast, lifting the dollar and December Fed hike odds; spot gold traded near $4,072.
MCX December gold rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g in the Muhurat session; silver edged up 0.2% to Rs 1,85,079 per kg.
Dhanteras gold and silver sales crossed Rs 60,000 crore, GJC estimated, up 15-20% in value on last year as buyers chose lighter jewellery.
Silver ended Friday at $51.89, up 5.75% on the week; JPMorgan and the World Bank trimmed 2027 forecasts.
US and Iran both reported ships hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz; US October CPI is due Tuesday 10 November.

brief.headline: Gold holds above $4,000 as Hormuz strikes stir haven bid
brief.summary: MCX gold rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g in Muhurat trade; spot gold near $4,072 as Hormuz ship strikes flared.

bullets.text: Strong US jobs data lifted the dollar and hike odds, Mint says, while Hormuz ship strikes kept safe-haven demand in view.
Dhanteras and Lakshmi Puja sales may cross Rs 62,000 crore, GJC said, as a price dip drew festive demand for lighter jewellery.
Watch: US October CPI on Tuesday 10 November at 19:00 IST; analysts say it and US-Iran tensions will set the tone next week.

trending.title: Jobs beat resets the Fed debate
trending.summary: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October, far above the 65,000 forecast, lifting the dollar and December hike odds; gold stayed above $4,000 and ended the week higher.

trending.title: Muhurat session caps a festive week
trending.summary: MCX gold rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g and silver edged up in the Diwali Muhurat session, closing a week in which bullion recovered from multi-week lows.

trending.title: Hormuz strikes keep safe-haven risk in view
trending.summary: Both the US and Iran reported ships hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, and analysts say US-Iran tensions will set the tone for bullion next week alongside US inflation data.

trending.title: Silver's strong week, cooler forecasts
trending.summary: Silver ended the week at $51.89, up 5.75%, but JPMorgan and the World Bank trimmed 2027 forecasts.

trending.title: Dhanteras demand, lighter buying
trending.summary: Dhanteras and Lakshmi Puja sales are estimated to cross Rs 62,000 crore, GJC said, but volumes stayed broadly flat as buyers chose lighter jewellery, small coins and quick-commerce deliveries.

items.title: Gold Price Today, November 8: Precious metals tick higher on MCX during Diwali special trading session
items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g in the Diwali Muhurat session, while silver futures edged up 0.2% to Rs 1,85,079 per kg after touching Rs 1,85,339. Spot gold held above $4,000 at about $4,071.67 an ounce and spot silver traded near $51.97.

items.title: Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
items.summary: Iranian media said blasts in southern Iran on Saturday evening were linked to Iranian military activity rather than US strikes, while both sides reported shipping hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines; the US said its air force disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

items.title: Gold, silver turn volatile after strong US jobs data, but remain on track to snap multi-week losing streaks
items.summary: MCX December gold fell ₹1,700 to ₹1,42,930 per 10 g and silver eased 1.26% to ₹1,84,800 per kg after US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above the 65,000 forecast, lifting the dollar and December Fed hike odds to 77%. Even so, gold is up nearly ₹4,000 this week and set to end a three-week losing streak, while silver is up over ₹5,700 for its first weekly gain in five weeks.

items.title: Bullion may remain under pressure as markets track US-Iran war, inflation
items.summary: MCX gold rose about 3% on the week to near Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 g and silver about 3.15% to near Rs 1.84 lakh per kg, with COMEX gold at $4,074.9 an ounce. Analysts say US-Iran tensions, US inflation data and the Fed's next move will set the tone next week, with safe-haven buying possible if tensions flare.

items.title: Gold Price Today: $4,045 After Jobs Beat, CPI Next on 10 November, Bull $4,135, Bear $3,990
items.summary: Spot gold ended Friday at $4,045 an ounce, down about 1% after US payrolls rose 165,000 — far above the 65,000 expected — lifting the dollar and December Fed hike odds to about 80%. Gold still gained about 4.4% on the week. The US October CPI report, due Tuesday 10 November, is the next test.

items.title: Silver Price Today: $51.89 After a 5.75% Week, CPI Due 10 November, Bull $55, Bear $49
items.summary: Silver ended Friday at $51.89 an ounce, up 5.75% on the week from $49.07, its 12-month low on 30 October. FinanceFeeds puts its bull case at $55 and bear case at $49, with the US October CPI due on Tuesday 10 November the next big test.

items.title: Gold sales during Dhanteras, Lakshmi Puja may cross Rs 62,000 crore
items.summary: Gold sales across India during Dhanteras and Lakshmi Puja are estimated to cross Rs 62,000 crore, the All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said on Sunday, reflecting strong festive demand despite elevated prices. GJC said gold returned about 9-14% between last year's Lakshmi Puja and this November, with prices now around Rs 1.42-1.43 lakh per 10 g.

items.title: Gold price holds critical $4,000 support, but strong U.S. jobs data and inflation risks threaten recovery
items.summary: Gold held above $4,000 after the strong US jobs report, analysts told Kitco, with Saxo's Ole Hansen expecting the level to hold; Blue Line's Phillip Streible warned a hot US inflation print next week could cement December hike bets and push gold back below $4,000. US CPI is due Tuesday.

items.title: Gold's Central Bank Bid Holds the Floor as Rate Fears Weigh on the Tape
items.summary: Gold finished Friday at $4,063.65 an ounce, caught between heavy official-sector buying and a macro backdrop pushing yields and the dollar higher after strong US jobs data. The World Gold Council said central banks added a net 321 tonnes in the third quarter, 42% more than a year earlier, while gold ETFs took in 211 tonnes; total demand slipped 1% to 1,369 tonnes.

items.title: Gold Jewellery Hallmarking: Mandatory hallmarking extended to 398 districts across 26 States, UTs
items.summary: Mandatory hallmarking of gold jewellery now covers 398 districts across 26 states and Union Territories, up from 392, after the government notified a fresh amendment to the hallmarking order. All nine Delhi districts are now covered, and Uttar Pradesh leads with 41 districts.

items.title: Global Gold Prices Down 24% From Record. In India, It's Down 20%. Here's What Makes Up The Difference
items.summary: Spot gold closed at $4,068.71 an ounce, about 24% below its Jan 29 record of $5,379, while Delhi gold fell only about 20% from its record. NDTV Profit puts the gap down to the duty rising from 6% to 15% in May and a rupee about 2% weaker since January, plus a January premium that has since vanished. The World Gold Council expects India's demand near 650 tonnes this year, the lowest since 2020.

items.title: World Bank's Gold Forecast For 2028 Is Almost Exactly Today's Price
items.summary: The World Bank expects gold to average $4,000 an ounce in 2028 — barely below Friday's spot close of $4,068.71 — after $4,600 in 2026 and $4,250 in 2027. The bank cites tighter monetary policy, higher yields and a firmer dollar; the figures are annual averages, not end-year targets.

items.title: Silver May Rebound Faster Than Gold, Ajay Kedia Sees ₹3 Lakh By Next Diwali
items.summary: Silver has corrected sharply from its January peak of Rs 4.20 lakh per kg to around Rs 1.90 lakh, and Kedia Advisory's Ajay Kedia expects it to recover faster than gold, moving towards Rs 2.80-3 lakh by next Diwali, while cautioning that volatility will continue.

items.title: Gold near interim bottom, but World Gold Council says three conditions associated with price recovery 'already in place'
items.summary: The World Gold Council says gold may be nearing an interim bottom, with two of three historical recovery signals in place: gold about 10% below its 200-day average and a strong dollar. Speculative positioning remains elevated, so the third signal is missing. Gold closed October at $3,913, down 6.3% in the month.

items.title: Goldman Sachs expects $7.5 billion of gold and silver buying from January index rebalancing
items.summary: Goldman Sachs' commodities desk expects the January 2027 rebalancing of the GSCI and Bloomberg commodity indices to generate $7.5 billion of buying in gold and silver — $4.51 billion in gold and $3.04 billion in silver — reversing three years of index-driven selling. Most trades are expected between the fifth and ninth business days of January; the bank notes it is a passive index adjustment.

items.title: ETF Gold Flows Slow In October But Remain Positive
items.summary: Global gold ETFs added a net 19 tonnes of gold worth $2.7 billion in October, taking holdings to a record 4,275 tonnes, though assets under management fell 6% to $542 billion as prices dropped. European funds led with 13.1 tonnes of inflows and Asian funds added 9.8 tonnes, while North American funds saw 4.5 tonnes of outflows.

Gold and silver sales crossed ₹60,000 crore on Dhanteras, the GJC estimated, with gold sales value up 15-20% on last year while volumes stayed broadly flat; silver sales rose 30% by value and 10% by volume. Jewellers from Kalyan to Senco reported higher footfalls and strong demand for lightweight jewellery and small coins after the price correction.
items.title: Dhanteras sales 2026: How much gold and silver did Indians buy this year
Dhanteras sales boom or price illusion? Why Indians spent more on gold and appliances without buying much more
items.summary: Dhanteras gold sales reached about Rs 60,000 crore, up 15–20% on last year, but the quantity sold was largely flat, jewellers' body GJC told PTI, with buyers choosing lighter jewellery, 18-carat designs and smaller coins. The World Gold Council's November 3 report showed India's September-quarter jewellery consumption down 20% year on year to 99.9 tonnes even as its value rose 16%.

items.title: India's silver import window opens as coin sales halve and London stocks build
items.summary: India has opened a simplified route for silver import licences covering about 6,500 tonnes over six months, which could ease supply in the world's most price-sensitive bullion market — if buyers use the permits. Physical demand stays muted, US Mint Silver Eagle sales fell 52% in September from a year earlier, and Metals Focus expects industrial silver demand to fall 3% in 2026.

items.title: China Extends Gold-Buying Streak to Two Years as Prices Drop
items.summary: China's central bank added about 830,000 ounces of gold in October, taking its buying streak to 24 straight months, even as bullion fell almost 7% in October to end below $4,000 an ounce. Purchases in the first ten months of 2026 total about 129 tonnes.

items.title: Global developments to keep commodity prices volatile in Samvat 2083
items.summary: Analysts expect geopolitics, global rates and supply-demand to keep commodity prices volatile in Samvat 2083. Anand Rathi's Vedika Narvekar sees MCX gold in a Rs 1.3 lakh-Rs 1.75 lakh range; Motilal Oswal's Navneet Damani sees $4,200 short-term and $4,500-4,700 medium-term. Silver, down over 55% from its record highs, could stay volatile with $48 as support.

items.title: India gold demand falls 29% in Q3 as record prices curb jewellery and investment buying: WGC report
items.summary: India's gold demand fell 29% year on year to 162.5 tonnes in the July-September quarter, the World Gold Council said, as record prices curbed jewellery and investment buying; in value terms demand still rose 3% to Rs 2.41 lakh crore, and the council sees full-year demand at 625-675 tonnes, a six-year low.

items.title: 14,000+ gold, silver coins delivered per hour: Instamart, Zepto, others record rising orders as Diwali shopping shifts to q-comm
items.summary: Zepto delivered more than 14,000 gold and silver coins an hour at its Dhanteras peak — about 298 coins a minute — its co-founder Aadit Palicha said. Swiggy Instamart saw gold coin orders jump 23 times in the week to Dhanteras, while silver coin orders rose seven times. Flipkart Minutes said gold coin and bar orders more than doubled.

items.title: Silver anklet units in Salem get a good amount of orders for this year’s Deepavali
items.summary: Salem’s silver anklet makers reported a sharp recovery for Deepavali, with orders rising to over 45%, nearly double the roughly 25% in 2025, The Hindu reported. The rebound followed silver easing to about Rs 2.05 lakh per kg from a volatile Rs 2.3–4 lakh range, and orders picked up in the last 15 days from buyers across five states.

items.title: NSE records 2.27 lakh Electronic Gold Receipts traded on Dhanteras
items.summary: NSE logged its highest-ever Electronic Gold Receipt volumes on Dhanteras, with 2,27,692 units traded, as festive buyers used the exchange-traded, dematerialised route to hold gold instead of taking physical delivery.

items.title: Silver Price Forecasts For 2027/28 Trimmed as Markets Shift
items.summary: JPMorgan cut its 2027 average silver forecast to $63.90 an ounce from $85.80, and the World Bank sees silver averaging $62 in 2027 and $58 in 2028, as solar makers use less silver per panel and physical tightness eases. Silver traded near $51, with the gold-silver ratio back at 78.
